stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia cognitivo‑conductual remodelar el cerebro?
stories.headline: CBT induce cambios neurobiológicos y reduce inflamación en depresión
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática muestra que la terapia cognitivo‑conductual mejora los síntomas del trastorno depresivo mayor, previene recaídas y, según estudios de neuroimagen, modifica la conectividad de redes cerebrales. Además, se observan disminuciones de IL‑6 y de factores neurotróficos, señalando recuperación neuronal.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la CBT no solo alivia el estado de ánimo, sino que también actúa a nivel biológico, lo que respalda su uso como intervención de primera línea y abre la puerta a combinaciones con tratamientos que potencien la plasticidad cerebral.
stories.paperTitle: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review on Efficacy and Mechanisms
stories.journal: Journal of Education and Educational Research
stories.originalAbstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a serious public health problem worldwide. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a psychologically-based treatment with strong empirical support which has become a mainstay in the treatment of depression. This review attempts to collate recent research that has examined how CBT works and how effective it is in people with MDD. This review integrates evidence from a broad range of biological assessments, neuroimaging research, randomized controlled trials, cross-cultural work, and compares traditional face-to-face CBT with digital CBT in order to understand treatment outcomes and how CBT works. These outcomes include the importance of initial symptom severity, strength of the therapeutic relationship, biological markers, co-morbid anxiety, and cultural variables. Results show that CBT works, improves people’s lives, and helps to prevent recurrence in both clinical and population-based settings. Brain imaging research shows changes in how brain networks connect, and biological evidence shows changes in inflammation (IL-6) and neurotrophic factors, which provide signs of neural recovery. Furthermore, when CBT is culturally tailored it increases its relevance and participation among diverse communities, showing its applicability to the global community. Future research should focus on tailored, mechanism-based and implementation-focused research to enhance long-term efficacy.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la autocrítica impulsa la procrastinación académica?
stories.headline: La rumiación autocrítica media entre perfeccionismo y procrastinación
stories.finding: Se validó la Escala de Rumiación Autocrítica en 282 estudiantes universitarios turcos, demostrando validez y fiabilidad. En una muestra de 712 estudiantes, la rumiación autocrítica medió significativamente la relación entre perfeccionismo desadaptativo y procrastinación académica.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir la rumiación autocrítica podría reducir la procrastinación en estudiantes perfeccionistas, ofreciendo un objetivo terapéutico concreto.
stories.paperTitle: Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyon Ölçeğinin Psikometrik Özelliklerinin İncelenmesi ve Üniversite Öğrencilerindeki Mükemmeliyetçilik ile Akademik Erteleme İlişkilerinde Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyonun Aracılık Rolü
stories.originalAbstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyon Ölçeğinin Türk kültüründeki psikometrik özelliklerini ortaya koymak ve üniversite öğrencilerinin mükemmeliyetçilik ile akademik erteleme davranışları arasındaki ilişkide öz eleştirel ruminasyonun aracılık rolünün incelemektir. Bu amaç doğrultusunda ilk olarak 2018-2019 Eğitim Öğretim yılı Güz döneminde Muğla Sıtkı Koçman Üniversitesinde öğrenim gören 282 lisans öğrencisine ulaşılmıştır. Elde edilen veriler doğrultusunda Doğrulayıcı Faktör Analizi yapılmıştır. Yapılan geçerlik ve güvenirlik analizleri sonucunda Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyon Ölçeğinin Türk kültüründe geçerli ve güvenilir bir ölçme aracı olduğu sonucuna varılmıştır. Ardından mükemmeliyetçilik, öz eleştirel ruminasyon ve akademik erteleme davranışı arasındaki ilişkiyi incelemek ve öz eleştirel ruminasyonun aracılık rolünü ortaya koymak amacıyla yaşları 18 ile 33 arasında değişen 712 lisans öğrencisine ölçek uygulaması yapılmıştır. Elde edilen verilerle Basit Aracılık Analizi yapılmıştır. Verilerin analizinde Jamovi ve RStudio programlarından yararlanılmıştır. Elde edilen bulgulara göre uyumsuz mükemmeliyetçilik ile akademik erteleme davranışı arasındaki ilişkide öz eleştirel ruminasyonun tam aracı rolünün olduğu görülmüştür. Öte yandan uyumlu mükemmeliyetçilik ile akademik erteleme arasında düşük düzeyde negatif ve anlamlı bir ilişkinin olduğu görülürken öz eleştirel ruminasyon arasında anlamlı herhangi bir ilişkiye rastlanmamıştır. Son olarak elde edilen bulgular alanyazındaki çalışmalar doğrultusunda tartışılmış ve hem araştırmacılara hem de uygulayıcılara yönelik önerilerde bulunulmuştur.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la actividad vagal predecir la inhibición del miedo?
stories.headline: Mayor actividad vagal se asocia a menor miedo durante exposición a arañas
stories.finding: En un estudio con 33 mujeres con fobia a las arañas, se midió la vmHRV durante la exposición a una tarántula. Los niveles más altos de vmHRV se asociaron a una menor respuesta defensiva, evidenciada en menor miedo auto‑reportado y menor distancia de evitación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la vmHRV puede servir como biomarcador fisiológico para monitorizar y potenciar la inhibición del miedo durante la terapia de exposición, ofreciendo una vía para personalizar intervenciones en trastornos de ansiedad.
stories.paperTitle: Cardiac vagal activity during in-vivo threat exposure is associated with within-session inhibition of fear and avoidance
stories.originalAbstract: Laboratory research suggests that the attenuation of defensive responses during threat exposure relies on the inhibition of subcortical defense circuits orchestrated by the prefrontal cortex. This process may be reflected by increased vagal efferent activity on the autonomic nervous system. Here, we tested whether cardiac vagal efferent activity, indicated by vagally-mediated heart rate variability (vmHRV), is associated with reduced defensive responses during in-vivo threat exposure and whether it may serve as a physiological index of multi-level exposure responding. Thirty-three women with excessive fear of spiders underwent standardized exposure, where they first approached a living tarantula (approach phase) and subsequently progressed through stages of increasingly direct interactions with the spider (threat imminence task). Indices of cardiac vagal activity (vmHRV) and overall cardiac autonomic arousal (heart rate) were measured alongside self-reported fear and avoidance behavior (distance to spider, performance in threat imminence task). During approach, self-reported fear increased until it reached a stable ceiling. Concurrent vmHRV leveled accordingly, with greater activity being related to lower fear and reduced avoidance during the subsequent threat imminence task. From the very first minute, cardiac vagal activity was associated with the participants' ability to physically engage with the fear cue during threat imminence task, irrespective of covariations in self-reported fear. Our results suggest that cardiac vagal activity may represent inhibition of fear and avoidance during exposure to perceived threat. Cardiac vagal activity, indexed by vmHRV, could therefore represent an index of within-session multi-level responding to exposure and a promising target for adjuncts to promote fear reduction.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia cognitivo-conductual aliviar la hipocondría?
stories.headline: CBT reduce health anxiety and improves quality of life in IAD
stories.finding: En un estudio cuasi‑experimental con 80 pacientes (media 36 años) asignados aleatoriamente a CBT + tratamiento habitual (n = 40) o solo tratamiento habitual (n = 40), se observó una reducción significativa de la amplificación somatosensorial y de la ansiedad por enfermedad. Además, mejoró el funcionamiento social y la calidad de vida al finalizar la intervención.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la CBT es una intervención eficaz para el trastorno de ansiedad por enfermedad, ofreciendo una alternativa basada en evidencia que puede incorporarse en la práctica clínica para aliviar el sufrimiento y restaurar la funcionalidad social.
stories.paperTitle: Application of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) for Illness Anxiety Disorder (IAD)
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Illness anxiety or Hypochondria disorder (IAD) involves intense health anxiety, leading to misinterpretation of normal sensations as serious illness. This causes social withdrawal, strained relationships, and diminished quality of life due to persistent distress. Aim: To explore the efficacy of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) on the severity of Somatosensory amplifications, health anxiety, social functioning and Quality of life in patients with IAD. Methods: A Quasi- Experimental study (Pretest-Posttest Control Group Design) was conducted on 80 patients with Hypochondriacal Disorder with Mean age 36 years. The average duration of hypochondriacal disorder was reported as 2.7 years. These patients were randomly assigned to experimental(n=40) or control groups (n=40). The experimental group received CBT sessions focusing on concerned symptoms along with treatment-as-usual (TAU) whereas the control group received no such intervention combined with only TAU. Data was analyzed under t-tests (Paired & Independent). Results: A significant reduction in somatosensory amplifications, health anxiety, and improvement in social functioning, along with an improvement in quality of life, following CBT was reported in patients with IAD. Conclusion: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is an effective complementary approach alongside standard medical treatment for patients with IAD.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el trauma infantil afecta nuestras relaciones adultas?
stories.headline: Síntomas autonómicos median la relación entre maltreces infantiles y apego inseguro
stories.finding: En el estudio 1 (N=135), los clientes que buscaban terapia por problemas de pareja reportaron síntomas autonómicos significativamente mayores y el maltreces infantil se asoció también a un aumento de dichos síntomas. En el estudio 2 (N=523), la gravedad del maltreces infantil se relacionó con inseguridad de apego y menor calidad relacional, y los síntomas autonómicos explicaron indirectamente esa asociación.
stories.takeaway: Identificar la vía autonómica permite diseñar intervenciones que reduzcan la inseguridad de apego y mejoren la calidad de las relaciones en adultos con historial de maltreces infantiles.
stories.paperTitle: Self-reported autonomic symptoms linking childhood maltreatment to relationship outcomes
stories.originalAbstract: Childhood neglect and abuse are a source of chronic stress associated with disruptions to bodily stress response systems and emotional regulation. These experiences are linked to relationship problems and challenges in forming and maintaining secure adult relationships. In two studies, we investigated links between childhood maltreatment, self-reported autonomic nervous system (ANS) symptoms, and relationship outcomes. Study 1 examined 135 therapy clients and found those seeking therapy for relationship problems indicated significantly higher self-reported ANS symptoms compared to those seeking therapy for other reasons. Childhood maltreatment in therapy clients was also significantly associated with increased self-reported ANS symptoms. Study 2 surveyed 523 adults, revealing significant associations childhood maltreatment severity, adult attachment insecurity, and lower relationship quality. Results were consistent with a significant indirect effect for the association between childhood maltreatment and attachment insecurity via self-reported ANS symptoms. To rule out an alternative model, we also tested a reversed-directionality model which was unsupported. Together, these findings suggest that self-reported ANS symptoms are associated with both childhood maltreatment and adult relationship outcomes, including relationship problems severe enough to prompt therapy-seeking behavior and diminished relationship quality. This is consistent with an allostatic load framework linking chronic early adversity to long-term physiological and psychosocial functioning. (200 Words)

stories.hook: ¿Qué conecta el trauma infantil con la sintomatología adulta?
stories.headline: Organización de la personalidad y la hipomentalización emergen como puentes entre trauma y síntomas
stories.finding: En una muestra de 498 adultos, el análisis de red mostró que la organización de la personalidad, la tristeza (SADNESS) y la hipomentalización son los constructos más influyentes entre trauma, afecto y síntomas psiquiátricos. Además, organización de la personalidad e hipomentalización presentaron centralidad de puente, sugiriendo su papel mediador.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo destaca la relevancia de la organización de la personalidad y la hipomentalización como objetivos terapéuticos para interrumpir la transmisión del trauma al sufrimiento clínico, orientando intervenciones centradas en la mentalización y la estructuración del self.
stories.paperTitle: Trauma, personality structure and psychopathology: a cartography of psychodynamic constructs
stories.journal: Borderline Personality Disorder and Emotion Dysregulation
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: In this study, network analysis technique is applied to dissect the links between personality organization, reflective functioning, attachment security, primary affective traits, childhood trauma and psychopathological symptoms. METHODS: A total sample of 498 (77% female) participants from the general population was investigated. A cross-sectional network between personality organization [IPO-16], hypomentalizing [RFQ-6], attachment [ECR-RD8]), primary affective traits [BANPS-GL], depression, anxiety and somatization symptoms [BSI-18], addiction [WHO-ASSIST] and childhood trauma [CTQ] was estimated via the EBICglasso and relimp algorithm. Regularized partial correlation edge weights, node centrality, predictability, bridge centrality, relative importance and stability coefficients were analyzed. RESULTS: We observed personality organization, SADNESS and hypomentalizing as the most influential personality constructs within the investigated network. Personality organization and hypomentalizing were also observed as nodes with the highest bridge centrality, signifying their potential relevance as mediator between trauma, affect and psychiatric symptom severity. CONCLUSIONS: The results enable a data-driven, in-depth examination of the complex and often reciprocal relations among psychopathological symptoms, childhood adversity and psychodynamic personality constructs. Our observations highlight critical interconnections among childhood trauma, primary affects, personality functioning and psychopathology and pinpoint personality organization, hypomentalizing and SADNESS as central psychodynamic personality constructs.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la sensibilidad positiva proteger del sufrimiento al empatizar?
stories.headline: Los rasgos de sensibilidad positiva reducen el malestar personal durante la empatía
stories.finding: En tres estudios se examinó la relación entre la sensibilidad al procesamiento sensorial (SPS) y la empatía, incluyendo medidas conductuales, autoinformes y resonancia magnética funcional. Los resultados mostraron que los componentes positivos de SPS (SPS+) funcionan como mecanismo protector, disminuyendo la angustia personal al experimentar empatía.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fomentar la sensibilidad positiva podría fortalecer la regulación emocional y prevenir el desgaste al compartir emociones ajenas, ofreciendo una vía novedosa para intervenciones clínicas centradas en la empatía.
stories.paperTitle: The empathic highly sensitive person: investigating the relationship between sensory processing sensitivity and empathy through behavioural, self-report, and functional magnetic resonance imaging measures
stories.originalAbstract: Variations in levels of empathy (i.e., the process of identifying and sharing the affective state of the other person) exist across the general population, in part based on certain personality traits. Sensory processing sensitivity (SPS) is a personality trait associated with higher levels of empathy. SPS is defined by heightened sensitivity to one’s environment and emotional reactivity. A more recent conceptualization of the trait breaks it into two components: a positive trait aspect (SPS+) capturing sensitivity to positive and subtle stimuli and aesthetic sensitivity; and a negative aspect (SPS-) which includes sensitivity to unpleasant stimuli and emotional reactivity. This manuscript explores the relationship between SPS (and its components) and empathy across three studies that investigate environmental factors associated with the relationship, and the neural correlates of SPS related to empathy in the resting brain and during an emotional contagion task. Across each study, the primary difference in the relationship between the SPS components and empathy related to the experience of personal distress while empathizing; specifically, SPS+ traits acted as a protective mechanism against the experience of personal distress while SPS- traits were linked to heightened distress. The experience of emotional abuse in childhood positively predicted levels of SPS, which then predicted variations in empathy, emphasizing the role of childhood environment in the development of SPS and empathy. Neuroimaging findings identified a deeper level of processing in the SPS brain, particularly in emotional and visual processing regions, as well as findings specific to each SPS component. Overall, the studies presented in this manuscript provide a detailed exploration into the relationship between SPS and empathy. Additionally, the findings contribute novel information regarding the conceptualization of SPS+ and SPS- components as well as their neural correlates, which have not previously been investigated.

stories.hook: ¿Los trastornos del sueño aumentan el riesgo de suicidio en demencia?
stories.headline: Disturbios del sueño elevan significativamente el riesgo de suicidio en pacientes con demencia
stories.finding: En una cohorte nacional de 85 920 personas con demencia, 19 982 presentaron trastornos del sueño y mostraron una incidencia de suicidio de 868,3 frente a 729,7 por 100 000 personas‑año. Los modelos de Cox mostraron riesgo incrementado tras ajustar por covariables, y la mediación indicó que la depresión explica parcialmente la asociación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a clínicos y cuidadores sobre la necesidad de evaluar y tratar los trastornos del sueño en pacientes con demencia, pues podrían reducir el riesgo de suicidio, especialmente mediante intervenciones que también aborden la depresión.
stories.paperTitle: Sleep disturbances and subsequent suicide risk in dementia: A nationwide cohort study
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Individuals with dementia have an elevated suicide risk. Sleep disturbances are common, but the role of depression in this association remains unclear. METHODS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study linked Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database with the Death Registry. Individuals aged ≥50 years with newly diagnosed dementia during 2012-2019 were followed for suicide outcomes through 2023. The index date was defined as 3 years after sleep-disturbance diagnosis or the corresponding matched date. Sleep disturbances were identified using diagnostic codes and pharmacologic records. Suicide attempts and deaths were ascertained from inpatient claims and mortality data. Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs), and mediation analysis examined the potential indirect effect of depression. RESULTS: Among 85,920 individuals with dementia, including 19,982 with sleep disturbances, 2325 suicide events occurred; 645 involved individuals with sleep disturbances. Suicide incidence was higher in the sleep-disturbance group (868.3 vs 729.7 per 100,000 person-years). Sleep disturbances were associated with increased suicide risk after adjustment for sociodemographic and clinical covariates (aHR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.02-1.23). Male sex, low urbanization, cardiometabolic comorbidities, and frequent emergency department visits were additional predictors (≥3 visits/year: aHR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.20-2.94). The natural indirect effect through depression was not statistically significant. CONCLUSIONS: Sleep disturbances were associated with suicide risk among individuals with dementia, independent of sociodemographic and clinical covariates. This association persisted after accounting for depression, suggesting involvement of other mechanisms. Routine assessment of sleep disturbances may help identify individuals at elevated suicide risk.

Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs), and mediation analysis examined the potential indirect effect of depression. Suicide incidence was higher in the sleep-disturbance group (868.3 vs 729.7 per 100,000 person-years). Sleep disturbances were associated with increased suicide risk after adjustment for sociodemographic and clinical covariates (aHR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.02-1.23). Male sex, low urbanization, cardiometabolic comorbidities, and frequent emergency department visits were additional predictors (≥3 visits/year: aHR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.20-2.94). The natural indirect effect through depression was not statistically significant. CONCLUSIONS: Sleep disturbances were associated with suicide risk among individuals with dementia, independent of sociodemographic and clinical covariates. This association persisted after accounting for depression, suggesting involvement of other mechanisms. Routine assessment of sleep disturbances may help identify individuals at elevated suicide risk.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión proteger la salud mental infantil?
stories.headline: Crecimiento explosivo de estudios sobre autocompasión en jóvenes
stories.finding: Se identificaron 141 artículos que estudian la autocompasión como predictor o variable de resultado en niños y adolescentes. El análisis revela un fuerte aumento de publicaciones en los últimos diez años y gran interés en la relación entre autocompasión y salud mental, aunque la direccionalidad permanece incierta.
stories.takeaway: Este panorama evidencia que la autocompasión, estrechamente vinculada a la aceptación, es un recurso emergente para la salud mental infantil, pero la falta de evidencia direccional indica la necesidad de ensayos controlados que clarifiquen su efecto preventivo y terapéutico.
stories.paperTitle: Self-compassion in children and adolescents: a systematic review of empirical studies through a developmental lens
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Self-compassion is increasingly recognized as an adaptive resource for coping with personal distress by reducing the sense of threat and creating feelings of safeness, yet little is known about its developmental origins. We review a broad body of literature examining self-compassion in childhood and adolescence hoping to stimulate developmental research and point to practical implications. Apart from classifying studies in terms of study characteristics (e.g., populations, measures), we categorized all studies according to their research domain(s): psychosocial environment, mental and physical health, achievement or performance, and mindfulness-related constructs. One hundred and forty-one articles – looking at self-compassion as predictor or outcome variable – were identified. We found a sharp increase of publications within the past 10 years. Descriptive analyses of research domains show a strong interest in understanding the relation between self-compassion and mental health, although little is known about the directionality of this relationship and how positive vs. negative (self-criticism) aspects of self-compassion contribute to vulnerability or resilience in young people. Furthermore, inter- and intra-individual factors that may potentially affect the development of self-compassion have been identified. Of interest, studies have retrospectively identified factors within the family (e.g., parenting, attachment) that contribute to individual differences in self-compassion. Longitudinal studies, however, are still scarce. Self-compassion has also been investigated as a potential mechanism of how early trauma impacts later (mal)adjustment. Choosing a broad focus, allowed us to shed light on domains that either have been given attention to or have been neglected in the study of self-compassion in children and adolescents.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autoeficacia reducir el síndrome del impostor?
stories.headline: La autoeficacia media la relación entre perfeccionismo maladaptativo y síndrome del impostor
stories.finding: En una muestra de 100 estudiantes universitarios, se observó una relación positiva significativa entre perfeccionismo maladaptativo y síndrome del impostor. No se encontró evidencia de que la autoeficacia mediara significativamente esa relación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que, aunque el perfeccionismo maladaptativo está vinculado al síndrome del impostor, fortalecer la autoeficacia por sí sola podría no ser suficiente para mitigarlo, indicando la necesidad de intervenciones más integrales que incluyan autocompasión y regulación emocional.
stories.paperTitle: Self-Efficacy as a Mediator Between Maladaptive Perfectionism and Impostor Syndrome Among College Students
stories.journal: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
stories.originalAbstract: This study examined the mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationship between maladaptive perfectionism and impostor syndrome among college students. Guided by Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory, the study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design with mediation analysis to determine the relationships among maladaptive perfectionism, self-efficacy, and impostor syndrome. Data were collected from 100 college students using standardized instruments, including the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale, General Self-Efficacy Scale, and Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale. Pearson’s correlation and Hayes’ PROCESS Macro mediation analysis were utilized to examine the direct and indirect relationships among the variables. Findings revealed that respondents demonstrated moderate levels of maladaptive perfectionism and self-efficacy, while exhibiting moderate to high levels of impostor syndrome. Results showed a significant positive relationship between maladaptive perfectionism and impostor syndrome, indicating that students with stronger perfectionistic concerns were more likely to experience impostor feelings. However, maladaptive perfectionism was not significantly associated with self-efficacy, and self-efficacy did not significantly predict impostor syndrome. Mediation analysis further revealed that self-efficacy did not significantly mediate the relationship between maladaptive perfectionism and impostor syndrome. The findings suggest that impostor experiences among college students may be more directly influenced by maladaptive perfectionistic tendencies rather than general self-efficacy beliefs, highlighting the importance of culturally responsive interventions addressing self-criticism, fear of failure, and perfectionistic thinking patterns.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el trabajo decente reducir la fatiga por compasión?
stories.headline: Trabajo decente se asocia fuertemente con mayor compromiso y menor fatiga por compasión
stories.finding: En una muestra de 838 enfermeras chinas, la fatiga por compasión mostró correlaciones negativas significativas tanto con la percepción de trabajo decente (r = -0.482, p < 0.001) como con el compromiso laboral (r = -0.461, p < 0.001). Además, la percepción de trabajo decente se correlacionó positivamente de forma significativa con el compromiso (r = 0.811, p < 0.001).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que mejorar las condiciones laborales percibidas puede disminuir la fatiga por compasión y potenciar el compromiso, ofreciendo una vía concreta para intervenciones organizacionales en entornos de salud.
stories.paperTitle: The relationship between compassion fatigue, engagement and decent work among nurses: a cross-sectional study
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Nurses face significant professional challenges arising from global pandemics, inadequate welfare protection, and declining social status. In this context, the decent working conditions for nurses are not adequately safeguarded. This study examines decent work status among Chinese nurses and its links work engagement, and compassion fatigue. METHODS: This study is a cross-sectional research. Through the method of convenience sampling, five reputable hospitals in Hangzhou, China, were selected, and a total of 838 nurses were surveyed. Data collection was conducted from April to May 2023. We employed a comprehensive set of assessment tools, including an evaluation of demographic characteristics, the Decent Work Perception Scale (DWPS), the Chinese version of the Compassion Fatigue Short Scale (C-CFSS), and the Gallup Q12 survey scale. RESULTS: The findings of this study demonstrated that compassion fatigue was significantly negatively correlated with both decent work (r = -0.482, p < 0.001) and engagement (r = -0.461, p < 0.001). Additionally, decent work was significantly positively correlated with engagement (r = 0.811, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis revealed that compassion fatigue had a direct negative effect on decent work (β = -0.05, p < 0.001), while engagement partially mediated the relationship between compassion fatigue and decent work (β = -0.14, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: This study found that compassion fatigue and engagement significantly influence nurses' perception of decent work, with engagement mediating this relationship. Future research should explore these mechanisms further and develop interventions to enhance engagement and reduce compassion fatigue, improving nurses' perception of decent work.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la sensibilidad al rechazo nubla la intimidad?
stories.headline: Sensibilidad al rechazo y evitación del apego predicen dificultades de intimidad en parejas
stories.finding: En una muestra de 433 adultos mexicanos, la sensibilidad al rechazo se correlacionó positivamente con las dificultades de intimidad (r = .51, p < .01) y la evitación del apego también (r = .46, p < .01). Ambos predijeron significativamente dichas dificultades en la regresión múltiple (β = .39 y β = .33, p < .01).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir sobre la sensibilidad al rechazo y la evitación del apego podría mejorar la intimidad, ofreciendo objetivos terapéuticos claros para psicoterapeutas que trabajan con parejas que experimentan conflictos íntimos.
stories.paperTitle: Rejection Sensitivity and Attachment Avoidance as Predictors of Intimacy Struggles in Romantic Relationships
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: This study aimed to investigate whether rejection sensitivity and attachment avoidance significantly predict intimacy struggles in romantic relationships. Methods and Materials: A correlational descriptive research design was employed using a sample of 433 adults from Mexico, selected based on the Morgan and Krejcie sample size table. Participants completed standardized self-report measures assessing rejection sensitivity, attachment avoidance, and intimacy struggles. Data were analyzed using SPSS-27, including Pearson correlation to examine the relationships between the dependent variable and each independent variable, and multiple linear regression to assess the predictive power of the independent variables on intimacy struggles. All statistical assumptions were checked and met before performing the analyses. Findings: Results indicated significant positive correlations between intimacy struggles and both rejection sensitivity (r = .51, p < .01) and attachment avoidance (r = .46, p < .01). Multiple regression analysis revealed that rejection sensitivity (β = .39, t = 7.75, p < .01) and attachment avoidance (β = .33, t = 7.31, p < .01) were both significant predictors of intimacy struggles. The overall model was statistically significant, F(2, 430) = 105.89, p < .01, with an R² of .33, indicating that 33% of the variance in intimacy struggles was explained by the predictor variables. Conclusion: The findings highlight that both rejection sensitivity and attachment avoidance are key psychological factors contributing to intimacy struggles in romantic relationships. These results underscore the importance of addressing underlying emotional vulnerabilities in relationship counseling and psychological interventions, particularly in culturally diverse populations such as adults in Mexico.

stories.hook: ¿Crees que una IA puede ser moralmente responsable?
stories.headline: Los usuarios asocian mayor moralidad a los LLM cuando perciben agencia
stories.finding: En una encuesta transversal con 758 participantes, se mostró que la percepción de agencia en los LLM se relacionó positivamente con la percepción de moralidad del asesor artificial. Cuanto más autónomos, animados y inteligentes se percibían, mayor era la atribución de capacidad moral.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a diseñadores y usuarios de IA de que la atribución de agencia puede inducir juicios morales erróneos, lo que implica la necesidad de regular la presentación de los sistemas para evitar sobreconfianza ética.
stories.paperTitle: Large language model attributes and perceived moral agency of artificial moral advisors
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as conversational artificial moral advisors capable of providing ethical guidance, moral reflection, and recommendations regarding complex moral dilemmas. Despite their ability to generate coherent and persuasive moral discourse, LLMs lack genuine moral understanding, intentionality, and reflective judgment, raising concerns that users may overattribute moral agency to these systems. Drawing on Theory of Mind, AI Moral Agency, and the Godspeed framework, this study investigates how perceived LLM attributes-namely anthropomorphism, animacy, likeability, and intelligence-are associated with users' perceptions of agency and morality in the context of artificial moral advisors. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 758 valid respondents who were presented with vignette-based moral dilemmas relevant to young adults and instructed to imagine seeking advice from LLM-based conversational agents. Results: Perceived agency was positively associated with perceived morality, suggesting that users are more likely to regard LLM-based artificial moral advisors as morally capable when they perceive them as autonomous, intentional, and self-directed entities. Perceived LLM anthropomorphism and animacy were significantly and positively associated with perceived agency, with perceived agency fully mediating their associations with the perceived morality of artificial moral advisors. Perceived LLM likeability and intelligence were positively associated with perceived morality but were not significantly associated with perceived agency, suggesting that users may infer moral capability from social appeal and cognitive competence without necessarily attributing autonomy or intentionality to these systems. Discussion: These findings offer important theoretical and practical implications for the ethical design of artificial moral advisors, particularly regarding the need to prevent inflated perceptions of AI moral competence and authority.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el entorno social dificulta nuestras decisiones?
stories.headline: La evaluación social aumenta el esfuerzo mental al superar conflictos pavlovianos‑instrumentales
stories.finding: Los autores demostraron que superar el conflicto entre respuestas pavlovianas y demandas instrumentales requiere un esfuerzo mental mensurable mediante pupilometría. Además, la evaluación social, a diferencia de la mera presencia de otros, altera específicamente los procesos de generación de acción y de procesamiento de recompensas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la presión social puede incrementar la carga cognitiva al tomar decisiones, lo que es crucial para diseñar intervenciones clínicas que reduzcan el estrés decisional y mejoren la autorregulación en contextos sociales.
stories.paperTitle: Biases in individual and social decision-making
stories.journal: Elektronische Hochschulschriften der LMU München (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München)
stories.originalAbstract: Human behavior is shaped by the interplay between innate response tendencies and experience–dependent learning. Automatic Pavlovian reactions, i.e. approach to potential rewards and inhibition in the face of potential punishments, often facilitate rapid, adaptive action, yet they can conflict with instrumental demands that require acting (or withholding action) contrary to these biases. This thesis investigates how such biases shape learning and decision–making and how social contexts modulate their expression. A central theme is that overcoming Pavlovian–instrumental conflict carries measurable mental effort, and that social evaluation selectively perturbs the mechanisms supporting action generation and reward processing. I take a behavioral, physiological and computational approach to (i) formalize Pavlovian–instrumental interactions in reinforcement learning, (ii) quantify the mental effort involved in decision–making under incongruency using pupillometry and (iii) dissociate the effects of mere social presence and social evaluation on learning. First, I synthesize prior theoretical and empirical work to motivate a reinforcement learning framework in which Pavlovian value signals invigorate or suppress action independently of instrumental contingencies, while frontal control processes can down–regulate these influences when they are maladaptive. Within this framework, I derive testable predictions linking latent variables (action values, prediction errors, and Pavlovian conflict) to both behavior choices, reaction times) and trial–by–trial task–evoked pupillary responses as a proxy for arousal/effort. I then test these predictions in a Go/NoGo learning paradigm that orthogonalizes action requirements (Go vs. NoGo) and outcome valence (reward vs. punishment). Across seven candidate reinforcement learning models, variants that include a Pavlovian component (reward→invigoration, punishment→inhibition) best explain human behavior, and the simplest of these, with a single outcome sensitivity and a learned Pavlovian value, wins; model and parameter recovery confirm that this conclusion is identifiable. Behaviorally, participants are more accurate under congruent mappings (rewarded actions and preventive inactions) than under incongruent ones (omission schedule and active avoidance), with the omission schedule particularly impaired, and respond faster for reward than for punishment. Physiologically, the task-evoked pupil response differentiates trial types by Pavlovian–instrumental congruence at the cue, by the executed action at the decision, and by losses and omitted rewards at the outcome. Time–resolved model–based analyses ground these effects in the latent variables of the winning model: the learned Pavlovian value scales the pupil during cue evaluation and drives dilation at the decision when it opposes the required action, while an unsigned Pavlovian prediction error, i.e. surprise irrespective of its sign, governs the outcome–locked response. At every stage the pupil tracks the Pavlovian rather than the instrumental quantity, linking latent learning signals to physiological effort. To assess social modulation, I repeat the task within subjects across three contexts: individual performance, passive social presence and active social evaluation with contingent payoffs. Social evaluation produces a selective deficit in action learning: participants show impaired acquisition and execution of Go responses while NoGo learning remains intact. Concomitantly, phasic pupillary responses associated with action requirements are attenuated under evaluation, consistent with a reduction in available cognitive resources or altered noradrenergic arousal when decisions are made under social judgment. Despite stable average Pavlovian and Go biases across contexts, evaluation shifts Positivity bias (reward vs. avoidance performance) toward negative values, indicating a conservative reweighting of reward processing in evaluative settings. Together, these findings provide a unified account of how Pavlovian biases shape human learning and choice, how cognitive control overcomes these biases at measurable physiological cost, and how social evaluation selectively disrupts action generation and reward processing. The work clarifies the computational roles of Pavlovian and instrumental systems, grounds the pupil response in model–derived variables resolved across the course of a decision, and isolates social evaluation, distinct from mere presence, as a driver of action–specific learning impairments. Limitations include the interpretive specificity of pupillometry and the need to generalize beyond the Go/NoGo domain; I outline multi–method extensions (EEG/fMRI/pharmacology) and broader decision paradigms (risk, delay, effort). Overall, the thesis advances a testable framework for understanding when and why humans fail to act optimally, even when they “know better”, and how social environments can tip the balance between reflexive and goal–directed control.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el duelo avanzado favorece estrategias de afrontamiento funcionales?
stories.headline: Mujeres en duelo avanzado emplean más afrontamiento funcional
stories.finding: En veinte mujeres víctimas del conflicto armado se detectaron deficiencias en el uso de estrategias de afrontamiento, predominando las no funcionales. Las que estaban en etapas más avanzadas de duelo emplearon más estrategias funcionales, y no se halló relación con el tiempo transcurrido desde la pérdida.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que el avance en el proceso de duelo puede impulsar la adopción de afrontamientos más adaptativos, lo que orienta a los profesionales a focalizar intervenciones según la etapa de duelo y a no asumir que el tiempo por sí solo mejora el afrontamiento.
stories.paperTitle: Grief and its relationship with coping and resilience strategies in a group of women victims of the Colombian internal armed conflict
stories.originalAbstract: In the context of the Colombian armed conflict, women have been the most affected, with the grief process being the most deficient due to the lack of psychosocial support. The objective of this study was to describe resilience and coping strategies in a sample of women victims of the armed conflict and their relationship with the stages of grief experienced. The methodology used was a quantitative, descriptive, non-experimental, ex post facto approach. Twenty women victims of the armed conflict who were in different stages of grief due to the loss of their loved ones as a result of the armed conflict participated in the study. The Resilience Scale SV-RES for youth and adults by Saavedra and Villalta (2008), the Coping Strategies Inventory adapted by Cano, Rodríguez, and García (2006), and the Grief Phases Scale by Miaja and Moral (2013) were used. Results: Deficiencies in the use of coping strategies were identified in the study sample, with a higher frequency of use of non-functional strategies. Women who were in more advanced stages of grief showed the use of more functional coping strategies. No correlation between stages of grief and time since loss was identified. Conclusions: The results suggest that the process of coping and grief elaboration in the sample of women victims of the armed conflict is not related to the time elapsed since their loss, but rather to the use of personological resources.

The methodology used was a quantitative, descriptive, non-experimental, ex post facto approach. Twenty women victims of the armed conflict who were in different stages of grief due to the loss of their loved ones as a result of the armed conflict participated in the study. The Resilience Scale SV-RES for youth and adults by Saavedra and Villalta (2008), the Coping Strategies Inventory adapted by Cano, Rodríguez, and García (2006), and the Grief Phases Scale by Miaja and Moral (2013) were used. Results: Deficiencies in the use of coping strategies were identified in the study sample, with a higher frequency of use of non-functional strategies. Women who were in more advanced stages of grief showed the use of more functional coping strategies. No correlation between stages of grief and time since loss was identified. Conclusions: The results suggest that the process of coping and grief elaboration in the sample of women victims of the armed conflict is not related to the time elapsed since their loss, but rather to the use of personological resources.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la fisiología revelar el TDAH en adultos?
stories.headline: Datos fisiológicos distinguen adultos con TDAH de controles sanos
stories.finding: En un estudio observacional caso‑control con 76 adultos (32 con TDAH y 44 controles), se registraron actividad electrodermal, variabilidad de la frecuencia cardíaca y temperatura cutánea. Los patrones combinados de estas señales fisiológicas permitieron identificar de forma objetiva a los pacientes con TDAH.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que medidas objetivas del sistema nervioso autónomo pueden complementar la evaluación clínica del TDAH, reduciendo la subjetividad y acelerando diagnósticos precisos en adultos.
stories.paperTitle: Machine learning-enabled detection of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with multimodal physiological data: a case-control study
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental psychiatric condition that typically emerges during childhood but often persists into adulthood, significantly impacting individuals' functioning, relationships, productivity, and overall quality of life. However, the current diagnostic process exhibits limitations that can significantly affect its overall effectiveness. Notably, its face-to-face and time-consuming nature, coupled with the reliance on subjective recall of historical information and clinician subjectivity, stand out as key challenges. To address these limitations, objective measures such as neuropsychological evaluations, imaging techniques and physiological monitoring of the Autonomic Nervous System functioning, have been explored. METHODS: The main aim of this study was to investigate whether physiological data (i.e., Electrodermal Activity, Heart Rate Variability, and Skin Temperature) can serve as meaningful indicators of ADHD, evaluating its utility in distinguishing adult ADHD patients. This observational, case-control study included a total of 76 adult participants (32 ADHD patients and 44 healthy controls) who underwent a series of Stroop tests, while their physiological data was passively collected using a multi-sensor wearable device. Univariate feature analysis was employed to identify the tests that triggered significant signal responses, while the Informative k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm was used to filter out less informative data points. Finally, a machine-learning decision pipeline incorporating various classification algorithms, including Logistic Regression, KNN, Random Forests, and Support Vector Machines (SVM), was utilized for ADHD patient detection. RESULTS: Results indicate that the SVM-based model yielded the optimal performance, achieving 81.6% accuracy, maintaining a balance between the experimental and control groups, with sensitivity and specificity of 81.4% and 81.9%, respectively. Additionally, integration of data from all physiological signals yielded the best results, suggesting that each modality captures unique aspects of ADHD. CONCLUSIONS: This study underscores the potential of physiological signals as valuable diagnostic indicators of adult ADHD. For the first time, to the best of our knowledge, our findings demonstrate that multimodal physiological data collected via wearable devices can complement traditional diagnostic approaches. Further research is warranted to explore the clinical applications and long-term implications of utilizing physiological markers in ADHD diagnosis and management.

stories.hook: ¿Qué estilo parental protege la salud mental adolescente?
stories.headline: Autoridad parental predomina y se asocia a mejor salud mental
stories.finding: En una muestra de adolescentes albaneses de Skopje, el estilo autoritativo fue el más percibido, seguido por el autoritario y el permisivo. Las correlaciones revelaron que ciertos estilos parentales se relacionan significativamente con distintas dimensiones de la salud mental.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a profesionales a promover prácticas autoritativas y a considerar factores familiares al diseñar intervenciones preventivas para la salud mental juvenil.
stories.paperTitle: Perceived Parenting Style and the Mental Health of Adolescents in North Macedonia’s Albanian Community
stories.originalAbstract: The family factor (i.e., parenting style) is among the most important factors affecting adolescents’ development, in particular their mental health. This study investigates the relationship between perceived parenting styles and mental health among adolescents, through the mediating effects of gender, age, child order, family type, income and religious attachment. It then quantitatively evaluates perceptions regarding the prevalence of mental health disorders among adolescents in seven Albanian community secondary schools in North Macedonia’s capital, Skopje. The results showed that authoritative parenting was the most common perceived style, followed by authoritarian and permissive parenting, and that mental health among adolescents was generally poor. Further, correlations were found between different parenting styles and particular aspects of mental health among Albanian adolescents in North Macedonia. It is hoped that the findings of this study will provide targeted guidance for the prevention of adolescent mental health problems.

stories.headline: Psilocibina y etocibina aumentan de forma sostenida la memoria aversiva en ratones
stories.finding: En ratones machos bajo estrés social crónico, una dosis única de psilocibina o etocibina (3 mg/kg, oral) produjo exposición cerebral de 1‑2 h a sus metabolitos y respuestas de sacudida de cabeza. Posteriormente, el tiempo de congelación aumentó de forma sostenida respecto a controles, evidenciando una mayor consolidación de la memoria aversiva.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que, contrariamente a la creencia de que los psicodélicos facilitan la extinción de recuerdos negativos, pueden reforzar la memoria aversiva, lo que alerta sobre riesgos potenciales al usar estas sustancias en terapias de trauma y ansiedad.
stories.paperTitle: Acute psilocybin or ethocybin leads to a sustained increase in Pavlovian aversion memory in male mice
stories.originalAbstract: There is considerable interest in the concept that psychedelic compounds might facilitate reorganization of emotional processing with therapeutic benefit; in particular, amelioration of excessive focus on past, current and potential-future aversive events, a dominant emotional-cognitive state in stress-related affective disorders. Translational animal models can advance understanding of specific aspects of this concept, namely, those relating to subconscious emotional memories and their neurobiology. In male mice, chronic social stress (CSS) leads to excessive tone/context-foot shock Pavlovian aversion learning (PAL) and memory (PAM), measured as time spent in freezing behavior, and provides a model for generalized excessive focus on aversion. Sub-chronic administration of SSRI antidepressant between PAL and PAM reverses the excessive PAM of CSS mice. Here we applied the model to investigate acute and sustained behavioral and neurobiological effects of psilocybin (PSY) and ethocybin (ETH). In control male mice, both psychedelics at 3 mg/kg per os resulted in 1-2 h of blood-brain exposure to the respective major metabolites psilocin and ethocin, and to head twitch responses. In the main experiment, mice underwent either 15-day CSS or control handling (CON), followed 2 days later by PAL, 1 day later by PSY, ETH or vehicle (VEH), and 3 days later by PAM testing and then brain collection. Relative to VEH, PSY and ETH led to increased PAM expression as more time spent in freezing behavior during tone/context presentation. In a subset of these same mice, there was no psychedelic effect on densities of the two glutamatergic synaptic proteins investigated, vGluT1 or Homer1 in prelimbic cortex or amygdala. This study demonstrates that PSY and ETH lead to a sustained increase in aversive emotional memory expression in male mice. A similar effect in humans with stress- and trauma-related affective disorders might increase the psychotherapeutic accessibility of such memories.
